title: Add Prompt Edit Delta Analyzer and CI advisor for regression attribution
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a lightweight prompt-edit delta analyzer and a CI advisor hook that attributes prompt-set regressions to one of three likely causes: prompt edits (author-introduced deltas), model changes (serving/model-version drift), or tokenization/tokenizer drift. This PR introduces a deterministic pipeline that computes per-example delta scores using a combination of n-gram overlap, embedding-based semantic drift, and tokenization diffs, produces a ranked list of candidate causes for each failing prompt, and surfaces suggested remedial actions such as revert-suggest, soft-rewrite suggestions, or tokenization normalization. The CI advisor runs a small canary sample for each PR, computes credible intervals over multiple stochastic seeds, and will annotate the PR with an explanation and an overall pass/fail decision if the aggregated regression is attributable >70% to prompt edits. The change includes unit tests, end-to-end smoke tests in CI, integration into the PR annotation workflow, and a short docs page on usage and limitations.
commit_summaries: Initial implementation of PromptEditDeltaAnalyzer core heuristic with ngram+embedding pipeline
Add CI hook to run analyzer on PR canary samples and post GitHub annotations
Add unit tests for attribution heuristics and deterministic tokenization diffing
Add end-to-end smoke test that exercises multi-seed aggregation and reporting
Documentation and developer guide for running analyzer locally and in CI

release_notes: Added Prompt Edit Delta Analyzer: automatic attribution of prompt-set regressions to prompt edits, model changes, or tokenization drift. Includes a CI advisor that annotates PRs with suggested remediation and configurable thresholds. Backwards compatible and disabled by default in enterprise installs.
notes: Rationale: many flaky regressions during model rollouts were due to inadvertent prompt edits; this tool aims to reduce time-to-blame and offer automated suggestions. Limitations: will not always pinpoint multi-cause failures and relies on representative canary sampling. Performance: a 100-sample run completes in ~9s on CI runners with caching enabled. Config: analyzer enabled via repo CI config under .github/prompt-delta-config.yml.
